title: add SLES/k3s-btrfs helpers and sparse-image indexer for air-gapped installs
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Customers running on-prem SLES clusters (SUSE Linux Enterprise Server) and k3s with btrfs root volumes hit two class of issues during air-gapped installs: (1) installer preflight fails because device setup/formatting expectations differ from ext4/overlayfs assumptions, and (2) the existing airgap image bundles are inefficient for sparse large layers produced by some SUSE base images. This PR introduces two complementary changes: a small set of SLES/k3s-btrfs helper scripts that normalize device preparation and systemd unit adjustments for k3s on btrfs, and a new 'sparse-image-indexer' helper that builds a compact index and manifest for vendored container blobs to reduce bundle size and speed registry bootstrapping in low-bandwidth environments. Description of changes: - installer: add distro detection for SLES and conditional device formatting hooks for btrfs-backed root /var/lib/kubelet volumes. New helper: scripts/sles/btrfs-prepare.sh (idempotent, uses lsblk+udevadm checks, preserves existing subvolumes). - packaging: vendor small set of systemd drop-in templates to tune k3s service on btrfs (no changes to upstream k3s). - bundler: introduce tooling/airgap/sparse-image-indexer.py that walks the OCI image blobs, computes per-blob sparse extents (for layers containing large zeroed regions), and emits a compact index (json) plus an optimized tar stream recipe that the offline registry daemon can consume to reconstruct blobs without sending zero ranges. - installer integration: the installer now recognizes an index.json in the airgap bundle and, if present, uses the sparse streaming path during registry replication. This path is safe-failable and falls back to the existing full-copy path on checksum mismatch. Backwards compatibility: existing bundles without index.json are handled unchanged. Rollout plan: feature-flags enabled in private-installer config until validated by a customer pilot. Testing: unit tests for the indexer, integration tests for the installer path using a k3s VM with btrfs root, and manual SLES 15 SP4 validation in our performance lab. Linkages: Linked Linear ENG-4122 for airgap optimizations and DEVOPS-78 for private installer distro support. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for indexer - [x] e2e scenario (local VM) - [x] docs: added README for sparse index format - [x] added release-note entry - [x] validated fallback path on checksum mismatch Security note: indexer runs offline during bundle generation and does not execute untrusted code at install time. See security considerations in PR body.

review_comments: Amit Patel: Nice direction. Two asks: (1) can the btrfs script avoid remount when not needed? (2) make sure sparse index format includes layer digest+size to avoid ambiguity.

Priya Shah (author): Addressed both. Script now checks mount options and early-exits when no action required; indexer emits digest+uncompressed_size+sparse_ranges. Added unit tests for the size field.
Lina Gomez: Integration test flaky on slow CI runners — timeout in replicator. Suggested adding an exponential backoff and a retry threshold.
Priya Shah: Added backoff and increased default timeout in replicator (configurable via feature flag). Verified in CI rerun.
ci_checks: integration-e2e: initial run failed on replicator timeout, rerun passed
security-scan: pass (no new executables with network at install time)
merge_details: Merged by squash on 2026-02-22 by release-manager using 'squash' strategy. Commit message summarized sles+btrfs support and sparse indexer. Merge included signed-off-by and changelog entry.
release_notes: Add SLES/k3s btrfs preparation hooks and a sparse-image-indexer to reduce airgap bundle sizes. Backwards-compatible and feature-flag gated.
testing_notes: Indexer unit tests exercise sparse ranges and digest matching. E2E VM tests validate btrfs device formatting without touching existing subvolumes. Manual validation performed on SLES 15 SP4 in lab.
